QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_25

question.text: In the 'Pay-for-success through Grants' structure (Figure 2.3), if the NPO achieves the pre-defined outcomes, the CSR funder typically releases the escrowed capital as follows:

answer.text: Partly to the interim funding partner (to cover its cost of implementing the programme) and partly to the NPO in the form of an accelerator grant up to 10% of the programme cost if the NPO exceeds the pre-defined outcome targets.
100% is paid to the NPO as a grant, and the interim funding partner writes off its contribution.
The CSR capital is rolled over to the next year regardless of performance.
The full amount is returned to the CSR donor.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.3.1.1(c), upon verified achievement the CSR funder pays the escrowed capital 'partly to the interim funding partner to cover the later's cost of implementing the program, and partly to the NPO in the form of an accelerator grant up to 10% of the program cost in case the NPO exceeds the pre-defined outcome targets'. The accelerator grant is designed to support non-programmatic areas (research, capacity building). The Trap: Option A ignores the interim funding partner's repayment claim. Option C describes the non-completion rollover, not success. Option D would defeat the purpose of the structure. Cross-Exam Context: V-A (MF Distributor), X-A/X-B (IA) treat CSR routing options. XIX-A/B/C/D/E (AIF) treat outcome-contingent waterfall mechanics. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When auditing a grants-in/grants-out structure, reconcile the CSR escrow statement, the interim funder's loan-repayment ledger, and the NPO's accelerator-grant receipt all to the same outcome-verification date — timing mismatches between these three legs is the most common audit finding.
